name: Xbox (Microsoft)
description: Xbox's biggest gamescom booth ever, celebrating 25 years of Xbox: 25 games on ~140 stations, a Fable live-demo theater, daily livestreams and an Xbox FanFest on Aug 26. Bethesda/Activision titles fold into this booth. Booth open Thu–Sun 9:00–20:00.

games.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4
games.note: First public 6v6 multiplayer hands-on — expected to be the single biggest queue of the show.

games.title: Gears of War: E-Day
games.note: First public campaign hands-on ahead of the Oct 6, 2026 release.

games.title: Fable
games.note: Live gameplay theater by Playground Games — not hands-on (reported release Feb 2027).

games.title: Minecraft Dungeons II
games.note: First public playable build.

games.title: METRO 2039
games.note: First hands-on anywhere; also at Plaion's Hall 9 booth.

games.title: Stranger Than Heaven
games.note: Sega/RGG Studio — also at SEGA's Hall 7 booth.

games.title: Halo: Campaign Evolved
games.note: Campaign remaster hands-on.

games.title: Forza Horizon 6
games.note: Drift Attack mode demo.

games.title: Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024
games.note: National Championship Air Races content.

games.title: Alien: Isolation 2
games.note: Also at SEGA's booth — compare queues.

games.title: Alien Deathstorm
games.note: Gameplay demo.

games.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker
games.note: Rebel Wolves' vampire RPG — also at Bandai Namco's booth.

games.title: STAR WARS Zero Company
games.note: Tactical strategy from Bit Reactor/Respawn.

games.title: Turok: Origins
games.note: Saber's co-op dino shooter.

games.title: Castlevania: Belmont's Curse
games.note: Also at Konami's Hall 7 booth.

games.title: Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy
games.note: Launches Aug 27 — mid-show.

games.title: Valor Mortis
games.note: Napoleonic soulslike from One More Level.

games.title: Crowsworn
games.note: Metroidvania demo.

games.title: Genigods: Nezha
games.note: Action demo.

games.title: Terrible Lizards
games.note: Demo at the booth.

games.title: Armatus
games.note: On the official Xbox Wire booth lineup.

games.title: Bad Magpie
games.note: Indie title at the booth.

games.title: Unannounced titles (~3 slots)
games.note: Xbox says 25 games but has named ~22 — reveals expected around Opening Night Live.

crowdNote: Largest platform booth of the show; MW4, Gears E-Day and the Fable theater will draw 2–4 h queues.
visitAdvice: Be at Hall 7 right at 9:00 opening Thu or Fri, head straight to CoD MW4 or Gears E-Day; do the Fable theater (higher throughput) mid-day. Avoid Saturday entirely.

name: Nintendo
description: Nintendo's traditional giant Hall 9 booth, all-in on Switch 2 with nine confirmed playable titles 'and more' — headlined by the first publicly playable Call of Duty on Nintendo hardware in over a decade (a native Switch 2 port).

games.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4
games.note: Native Switch 2 build (Infinity Ward + Digital Legends) — not cloud streaming.

games.title: 007 First Light
games.note: IO Interactive's Bond game, hands-on all five days.

games.title: EA Sports FC 27
games.note: Full FC experience on Switch 2.

games.title: Metaphor: ReFantazio
games.note: Atlus RPG port hands-on.

games.title: Minecraft Dungeons II
games.note: Switch 2 version; also at the Xbox booth.

games.title: Nintendo Switch Sports Resort
games.note: First-party family title — big weekend draw.

games.title: Orbitals
games.note: Hands-on demo.

games.title: Pokémon Pokopia (Expansion Pass)
games.note: Expansion Pass content playable — expect huge Pokémon queues.

games.title: Splatoon Raiders
games.note: First-party spin-off hands-on.

games.title: Additional unannounced titles
games.note: Nintendo's announcement explicitly says 'and more'.

crowdNote: Historically the most-queued family destination at gamescom; MW4-on-Switch-2 novelty plus Pokémon and Splatoon mean 2 h+ waits, worst Sat/Sun.
visitAdvice: Thu or Fri at opening; hit MW4 or 007 First Light first. Nintendo often runs virtual queue tickets via booth/app — grab a slot early. Avoid the weekend.

name: PlayStation (Sony)
description: NOT exhibiting with a consumer booth — Sony skips a PlayStation booth for the seventh year running (last appearance 2019), favoring its own State of Play streams and Tokyo Game Show. Sony's only registrations in the official directory are trade- or partner-facing: SIE Deutschland on a shared industry stand in business Hall 4.1 (trade only), Sony Pictures co-located at Capcom's Hall 9.1 booth, and 'Sony Europe' plots on the open-air site north of Hall 8. PS5 titles are still playable at third-party booths (Blood of Dawnwalker, Turok, 007 First Light and more).
crowdNote: No booth to queue for.
visitAdvice: Don't look for PlayStation on the floor — play multi-platform PS5 titles at Xbox, Bandai Namco, SEGA and other publisher booths. A surprise ONL trailer is always possible.

name: Google Play
description: Officially listed in the 2026 exhibitor directory, near Xbox in Hall 7.1. Expect mobile and Google Play Games on PC partner titles, demo stations and giveaways; the specific lineup is still TBC.

games.title: Partner mobile/PC titles
games.note: Directory notes 'feature of developer IP TBC' — lineup unannounced.

crowdNote: Steady but modest traffic; queues mostly for merch and giveaways.
visitAdvice: Easy walk-in most of the day — convenient to combine with the Xbox booth in the same hall.

name: Capcom
description: One of Hall 9's biggest footprints (~950 m², ~60 demo stations) with two world-first hands-ons — Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen and Mega Man: Dual Override — plus Onimusha a week before launch. Rocket Beans runs the stage program.

games.title: Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen
games.note: World-first public hands-on of the expansion (launches Oct 9, 2026).

games.title: Mega Man: Dual Override
games.note: First playable demo of the 12th mainline Mega Man.

games.title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword
games.note: Playable weeks before its late-September release — likely the booth's biggest draw.

games.title: Street Fighter 6
games.note: Casual play stations and community matches.

crowdNote: Two world-first demos plus near-launch Onimusha in the most congested hall — expect 1–3 h queues for Dark Arisen and Onimusha.
visitAdvice: Go straight to Capcom at hall opening on a weekday: Dark Arisen first (fewest stations vs demand), then Onimusha. Street Fighter 6 queues stay short all day.

name: SEGA / Atlus
description: Trademark themed booth in Hall 7: Alien: Isolation 2's European hands-on debut in a claustrophobic sci-fi set, Persona 4 Revival in a recreated Junes shopping center, and Stranger Than Heaven staged as an underground jazz club.

games.title: Alien: Isolation 2
games.note: European hands-on debut of the prologue; also at the Xbox booth — compare queues.

games.title: Persona 4 Revival
games.note: First Western public hands-on, in a Junes-themed area.

games.title: Stranger Than Heaven
games.note: First public hands-on of RGG Studio's new game; jazz-club themed area.

games.title: Crazy Taxi: World Tour
games.note: Early hands-on with a brand-new city map.

games.title: Total War: Warhammer 40,000
games.note: Hands-on debut with three Space Marine scenarios.

games.title: Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds
games.note: Latest build incl. the TMNT pack.

games.title: Sonic Pico Park
games.note: New co-op Sonic title.

games.title: Metaphor: ReFantazio (Switch 2)
games.note: Also at Nintendo's Hall 9 booth.

games.title: Total War: Warhammer III – Lords of the End Times
games.note: Expansion showcase.

crowdNote: Three first-time hands-ons — long individual queues but the load spreads across a big varied lineup.
visitAdvice: Prioritize Alien: Isolation 2 or Persona 4 Revival first thing in the morning (Alien is also at Xbox — check both queues). Sonic and Crazy Taxi turn over fast and suit afternoons.

name: Bandai Namco
description: Fully playable lineup next to Ubisoft and EA in Hall 6, headlined by the world's first open hands-on of The Blood of Dawnwalker (out Sept 3) and the first playable Ace Combat 8, plus the usual spectacular photo-op builds.

games.title: Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve
games.note: First-ever public hands-on; launches Oct 2, 2026.

games.title: Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3
games.note: First playable in Europe; full release 2027.

games.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker
games.note: World-first open sessions days before its Sept 3 launch; also at the Xbox booth.

games.title: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition
games.note: Releases Aug 28 mid-show; floated by German trade press, not in the announced lineup.

games.title: One Piece: Grand Gourmet
games.note: Oct 23 release makes it a candidate; unannounced for the booth.

crowdNote: Three first-time hands-ons incl. a hot RPG launching during show week — Dawnwalker queues among Hall 6's longest.
visitAdvice: Hit The Blood of Dawnwalker at opening, or use the Xbox booth's stations in Hall 7 as overflow. Do Ace Combat 8 the morning after its ONL showing.

name: Konami
description: Main Hall 7 booth with an immersive Silent Hill: Townfall walk-through experience (new trailer at ONL), playable Castlevania: Belmont's Curse and a Metal Gear photo spot — plus a separate Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG stand in Hall 5.2 (B021/A020).

games.title: Silent Hill: Townfall
games.note: Interactive walk-through experience, not a demo; new trailer at ONL Aug 25.

games.title: Castlevania: Belmont's Curse
games.note: Playable throughout the show; also at the Xbox booth.

games.title: Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2
games.note: Photo opportunity in front of a Metal Gear unit.

games.title: Yu-Gi-Oh! Trading Card Game
games.note: Learn-to-play sessions at the Hall 5.2 card-game stand.

crowdNote: The Townfall experience will queue like a theme-park attraction after its ONL trailer; Castlevania concentrates the demo demand.
visitAdvice: Do the Silent Hill experience early Wednesday before ONL hype converts to foot traffic, or in the last hour of a day. Castlevania is also playable at Xbox — use the shorter queue.

name: Ubisoft
description: Traditional spot at the Hall 6 entrance with a playable Rayman Legends Retold demo plus the returning Community Lounge — developer talks and live-streamed sessions (Aug 26–29) around Rainbow Six Siege, AC Black Flag Resynced, Anno 117 and The Division 2.

games.title: Rayman Legends Retold
games.note: Demo: opening level, a new dragon-ride sequence and a classic musical level.

games.title: Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced
games.note: Community Lounge showcase of the Black Flag remake.

games.title: Anno 117: Pax Romana
games.note: Community Lounge sessions.

games.title: Rainbow Six Siege
games.note: Community Lounge sessions rather than a demo queue.

games.title: The Division 2
games.note: Live-service community sessions.

crowdNote: One playable title plus a lounge format — moderate queues, no giant new AAA hands-on this year.
visitAdvice: Rayman queues are manageable before noon on weekdays. Community Lounge sessions are schedule-based — check Ubisoft's channels for timings.

name: Electronic Arts
description: Officially back as an exhibitor (confirmed late July) with a booth at the Hall 6 entrance next to Ubisoft — but the lineup is still unannounced. EA Sports FC 27, launching weeks after the show, is the near-certain centerpiece.

games.title: EA Sports FC 27
games.note: Launches weeks after gamescom; Switch 2 version separately confirmed at Nintendo's booth.

games.title: Battlefield 6 (seasonal content)
games.note: German trade press says BF6 'may play a role' at the booth.

games.title: skate.
games.note: Live-service title in active rollout; plausible but unannounced.

crowdNote: FC 27 stations traditionally draw steady but fast-moving queues; busy rather than overwhelming without a big reveal.
visitAdvice: FC has many stations and short rotations — fine mid-day.

name: Square Enix
description: Late addition to the exhibitor list: a Final Fantasy-focused fan booth in Hall 8 with play stations, photo stops and a large merch range — a community/catalog showing, with Dragon Quest VII Reimagined the one genuinely new title.

games.title: Dragon Quest VII Reimagined
games.note: The booth's one new title — its only likely long queue.

games.title: Final Fantasy VII Rebirth
games.note: Play stations, likely new-platform versions.

games.title: Final Fantasy XIV
games.note: MMO community presence.

games.title: Final Fantasy X/X-2 HD Remaster
games.note: Catalog play station.

games.title: Final Fantasy VII Revelation
games.note: 'New Look' presentation at Opening Night Live (Aug 25) led by director Naoki Hamaguchi, with new footage — an ONL reveal segment, not a confirmed show-floor demo.

crowdNote: Strong brand pull but no world premieres on the show floor — steady traffic for photo ops and merch; the ONL FF7 Revelation reveal (Aug 25) may bring extra attention the next morning.
visitAdvice: Merch sells out early in the show — buy on your first pass. Good midday stop; combine with CD Projekt Red in the same hall.

name: CD Projekt Red
description: CDPR's first gamescom booth since 2019: extended theater presentations of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt — Songs of the Past (the newly announced third expansion, due 2027), running Wed–Sun after its trailer debut at Opening Night Live.

games.title: The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past
games.note: Cinema-style presentation, not hands-on; first trailer at ONL Aug 25; releases 2027.

crowdNote: CDPR theaters historically generate multi-hour lines (see Cyberpunk 2077 in 2019); a new Witcher reveal right after ONL will be a hall-wide magnet.
visitAdvice: Treat it like a timed show: queue at Hall 8 opening on Wed/Thu, or try the final showings late Sunday. Hall 8 sits at the North entrance — enter there, not via the Boulevard.

name: Gryphline (Arknights: Endfield)
description: Hypergryph's global publishing brand returns with a significantly bigger Arknights: Endfield presence across two Hall 8.1 stand blocks: expanded interactive installations and photo spots, plus Boss Speedrun Challenges with exclusive event rewards.

games.title: Arknights: Endfield
games.note: Boss Speedrun Challenge stations with exclusive event rewards.

crowdNote: Endfield's community is huge and last year's smaller booth was packed; challenge stations are the bottleneck.
visitAdvice: Do the speedrun challenge first thing — reward stock and queue caps bite by midday; the photo installations stay accessible all day.

name: Snail Games
description: The ARK publisher's officially announced stand (8.1, A-041): new ARK: Survival Ascended content alongside open-universe MMO For The Stars, medieval survival sim Bellwright and cozy builder Honeycomb: The World Beyond — plus a first public look at an unannounced, internally developed AAA title.

games.title: ARK: Survival Ascended
games.note: New content and franchise developments for the survival flagship.

games.title: For The Stars
games.note: Open-universe MMO.

games.title: Bellwright
games.note: Medieval survival/colony sim, 1M+ players on Steam.

games.title: Honeycomb: The World Beyond
games.note: Sci-fi sandbox builder; also on Snail's official gamescom profile.

games.title: Unannounced Snail AAA title
games.note: First look promised for media and attendees.

crowdNote: ARK's community is large and a AAA reveal pulls walk-up interest, but it's a mid-size stand rather than a mega-booth.
visitAdvice: If the unannounced title lands a splashy reveal, the stand will busy up the next morning — otherwise ARK fans can drop in most times.

name: Plaion (Deep Silver)
description: One of Hall 9's largest booths, centered on METRO 2039 from in-house studio 4A Games — additionally playable at the Xbox booth in Hall 7.

games.title: METRO 2039
games.note: Focus title; also at Xbox's Hall 7 stand.

crowdNote: A single high-profile shooter concentrates demand, but dual-location availability splits the queues.
visitAdvice: Compare queues at Plaion (Hall 9) vs Xbox (Hall 7) — Xbox's 140 stations often move faster.

name: KRAFTON
description: One of Hall 9's largest presences with five titles, headlined by a still-secret world-premiere FPS from PUBG STUDIOS (set in the Pacific Northwest) plus Neon Giant's cyber-noir shooter NO LAW. Interactive missions earn themed merch. The location is now officially confirmed in the exhibitor directory, with two stand blocks: B050/C051 plus B040/C041.

games.title: Untitled PUBG STUDIOS project
games.note: World-premiere reveal of a new PUBG-universe FPS at the show.

games.title: NO LAW
games.note: Open-world FPS from The Ascent developer Neon Giant — hands-on demo.

games.title: Project ZETA
games.note: Part of the five-title showcase.

games.title: Age Twisters
games.note: Part of the five-title showcase.

games.title: TARAE: The Unbound
games.note: Dark-fantasy action RPG.

crowdNote: A PUBG-universe world premiere in the show's most congested hall guarantees heavy traffic once the reveal lands.
visitAdvice: Visit Wednesday/Thursday morning before the PUBG premiere is fully publicized; do the merch mission circuit early before stock runs low.

name: Embark Studios
description: Riding ARC Raiders' breakout success, the Swedish studio booked a Hall 6 booth reportedly twice the size of EA's — a first-time flex centered on its extraction-shooter hit.

games.title: ARC Raiders
games.note: Booth focus; expect new-content showcases for the live-service hit.

games.title: THE FINALS
games.note: Embark's other live title; not yet listed for the booth.

crowdNote: Massive active player base and a first big booth — community turnout plus any new-season reveal will pack it.
visitAdvice: Community events and creator meetups spike traffic unpredictably — check Embark's socials for the stage schedule and go during downtime.

name: Team17 × astragon
description: Shared group booth (officially B060/C061, a stand block also shared with Focus Entertainment): Team17's creature-collector LumenTale and Silver Pines alongside astragon's simulator lineup (Bus Simulator 27, Construction Simulator Evolution, Firefighting Simulator: Ignite).

games.title: LumenTale: Memories of Trey
games.note: Team17's headline demo.

games.title: Silver Pines
games.note: Second confirmed Team17 title.

games.title: Bus Simulator 27
games.note: astragon side; launches days after the show.

games.title: Construction Simulator Evolution
games.note: astragon simulator lineup.

games.title: Firefighting Simulator: Ignite
games.note: astragon simulator lineup.

crowdNote: Indie-scale titles at a shared booth — queues short outside peak Saturday hours.
visitAdvice: An easy low-queue stop while waiting out timed queues elsewhere in Hall 6.

name: GIANTS Software
description: Farming Simulator's developer-publisher with its traditional community booth (plus a business-area stand in Hall 4.2). The booth program is unannounced so far — Farming Simulator 26 (Switch/mobile, out May 2026) and FS25 expansion content fresh from FarmCon are the safe bets, alongside merch.

games.title: Farming Simulator 26
games.note: The Switch/mobile edition released May 19, 2026 — likely demo stations.

games.title: Farming Simulator 25: Beans & Alpacas
games.note: First gameplay was shown July 28 at FarmCon; a gamescom showing fits its pre-release window.

crowdNote: One of the most loyal German communities at the show — steady all-day traffic rather than spike queues.
visitAdvice: Easy to combine with the surrounding Hall 6.1 AAA booths; merch tends to sell out on weekend days.

name: Focus Entertainment
description: Booth officially confirmed in the gamescom exhibitor directory: Hall 6.1, B060/C061 — a stand block it shares with Team17 and astragon. Its big release Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy launches Aug 27 — mid-show — and is confirmed playable at the Xbox booth.

games.title: Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy
games.note: Launches Aug 27; confirmed at Xbox's Hall 7 booth, likely also at Focus' own Hall 6.1 stand.

games.title: Edge of Memories
games.note: 2026 JRPG-style title, plausible booth candidate.

games.title: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 3
games.note: Too early for hands-on; trailer presence possible.

crowdNote: No announced blockbuster hands-on at its own stand; Resonance demand mostly absorbed by the Xbox booth.
visitAdvice: Queue for Resonance at the Xbox booth where it's confirmed playable. Focus' own Hall 6.1 stand (B060/C061) is reported by trackers but not yet Focus-confirmed — double-check the official exhibitor directory closer to the show.

name: HoYoverse
description: One of the biggest Asian booths of the show (~660 m², plus a business booth in Hall 4.2): five titles across themed zones — a Snezhnaya-themed Genshin area, Honkai: Star Rail's Planarcadia, Zenless Zone Zero, and world-premiere hands-ons for Honkai: Nexus Anima and Petit Planet.

games.title: Genshin Impact
games.note: Snezhnaya-themed zone with railway and Statue of The Seven builds; exclusive merch.

games.title: Honkai: Star Rail
games.note: Planarcadia-themed zone (Version 4.4 era).

games.title: Zenless Zone Zero
games.note: Dedicated exhibition area with latest content.

games.title: Honkai: Nexus Anima
games.note: World-premiere hands-on of the new creature-collecting strategy game.

games.title: Petit Planet
games.note: Cozy life-sim hands-on with world exploration.

crowdNote: Historically among the longest queues at gamescom — limited-edition merch reliably produces 1–3 h lines and capacity-controlled entry, especially Sat/Sun.
visitAdvice: Go at hall opening Thu/Fri and head straight for the merch counter or the Nexus Anima demo; photo zones are easier mid-afternoon. Budget half a day for demos plus merch.

name: Level Infinite (Tencent)
description: Tencent's global publishing brand, next door to HoYoverse, with a fully playable three-game lineup headlined by the world-first public hands-on of Remedy's CONTROL Resonant. Themed photo spaces, prize wheel, dev meet-and-greets and a Hunt: Showdown cosplay showcase.

games.title: CONTROL Resonant
games.note: First time playable anywhere; launches Sept 24, 2026 — the booth's biggest draw.

games.title: Dune: Awakening (console)
games.note: First public hands-on of the console build.

games.title: Hunt: Showdown 1896
games.note: Playable with devs present; new in-game event preview.

crowdNote: CONTROL Resonant's world-first demo two months before launch will pull 60–120 min lines; adjacency to HoYoverse makes Hall 6.1 one of the most congested areas.
visitAdvice: Queue for CONTROL Resonant first thing in the morning; Dune and Hunt stations move faster and are fine late afternoon.

name: Tencent — Worlds of Play
description: Tencent Games is officially registered on the show floor — Hall 8.1, B050/A051, program still unannounced — in addition to 'Worlds of Play: The Game Art Exhibition' offsite at the Wassermannhalle (Aug 27–29): five themed zones spanning art from 40 titles, developer talks and cosplay showcases. Tencent's playable games remain at Level Infinite in Hall 6.1.

games.title: Worlds of Play (40-title art exhibition)
games.note: Art exhibition Aug 27–29, off the main show floor.

games.title: Tencent Hall 8.1 booth (program TBA)
games.note: Officially registered stand at 8.1 B050/A051 — what's shown there hasn't been announced yet.

crowdNote: Timed/curated and off the main floor — moderate queues; the real crowds gather at Level Infinite.
visitAdvice: A calmer palate-cleanser between hall sessions; check whether entry needs free time-slot registration closer to the show.

name: NetEase Games
description: Officially confirmed by NetEase's own Aug 11 press release: Hall 7.1 booth A-051 for Sea of Remnants, and booth B-050 for Marvel Rivals (Season 9.5 content, Jeff the Landshark statue, photo booth) and Where Winds Meet's Hidden Mountain finale. NetEase also runs a separate trade-only stand in the Business Area (Hall 4.2, D-050) previewing Once Human's next expansion plus one unannounced title.

games.title: Marvel Rivals
games.note: Multi-station 6v6 setups; Season 9.5 content at booth B-050.

games.title: Where Winds Meet
games.note: Wuxia open-world RPG; Hidden Mountain finale content at booth B-050.

games.title: Sea of Remnants
games.note: Stylized pirate adventure RPG, own booth A-051; hands-on status not detailed in NetEase's release.

games.title: Once Human next expansion + unannounced title
games.note: Hands-on preview at NetEase's Business Area stand (Hall 4.2, D-050) — trade & media only, not reachable on a public ticket.

crowdNote: Marvel Rivals is one of the biggest live-service shooters right now; 6v6 sessions cycle slowly — 45–90 min waits at peak.
visitAdvice: Marvel Rivals seats 12 per cycle, so lines move in bursts — join right after a session starts. Sea of Remnants is at a separate booth (A-051) from Marvel Rivals/Where Winds Meet (B-050), both in Hall 7.1 near Xbox.

name: Pearl Abyss
description: Showcasing Crimson Desert (6M+ sales) in partnership with Samsung: 30 demo PCs on Samsung's new 6K Odyssey G8 monitors, plus stage events, giveaways and cosplay. Officially at 9.1 B010/C011 (an earlier revision had this swapped with Samsung's own stand); Samsung is co-registered here as the tech partner.

games.title: Crimson Desert
games.note: Current release build on 30 Samsung Odyssey G8 6K/165 Hz stations.

crowdNote: 30 stations give decent throughput, but the 6K showcase plus a hit game means steady 30–60 min lines, longer on the weekend.
visitAdvice: The 30-station setup clears queues faster than most AAA booths — late morning Thu/Fri is a good window.

name: Infold Games
description: Publisher of Infinity Nikki and Love and Deepspace. The Infinity Nikki booth (officially announced as 9-A054) hosts meet-and-greets with Nikki and Momo, activity stations with exclusive merch rewards and special events with guest appearances; Love and Deepspace shared Infold's booth in 2025 and is expected back.

games.title: Infinity Nikki
games.note: Official booth events, activities and exclusive merch — expect activity queues rather than demo stations.

games.title: Love and Deepspace
games.note: Not yet officially named for 2026; shared the Infold booth last year.

crowdNote: Both games have enormous, dedicated fandoms; merch and photo-op lines at comparable booths ran 60+ minutes in 2025.
visitAdvice: Go at hall opening for limited daily merch and event slots — activity rewards tend to run out by early afternoon on public days.

name: Aerosoft
description: The Paderborn simulation specialist confirms Winter Resort 3 and Professional Ship Simulator, plus five simulators revealed for the first time at the show — police work, mining, firefighting, crab fishing and roadmaking. A compact stand among Hall 9.1's big booths (plus a business-area stand in 4.2).

games.title: Winter Resort 3
games.note: Alpine ski-resort sim sequel.

games.title: Professional Ship Simulator
games.note: Part of the confirmed lineup.

games.title: Five unannounced simulators
games.note: First reveals: police work, mining, firefighting, crab fishing and roadmaking.

crowdNote: Dedicated sim niche — steady interest but rarely long lines.
visitAdvice: Pairs into a sim circuit with GIANTS and the Team17 × astragon stand in Hall 6.1; reveal stations are busiest right after doors.

name: Grinding Gear Games
description: Path of Exile 2 booth confirmed at Hall 6.1, B031 (two independent trackers, nat-games.de and gamesfinest.de, Aug 11) with an event-exclusive special demo, an 'eerie display' photo op and exclusive merchandise.

games.title: Path of Exile 2
games.note: Special demo exclusive to gamescom, post-'Return of the Ancients' era.

crowdNote: Very large, dedicated European PC-ARPG audience and a venue-exclusive demo — long, steady lines plus merch demand.
visitAdvice: Hit it early on a weekday; ask staff whether merch has a separate line from the demo queue.

name: Eclipse Glow Games
description: Chinese studio behind Arthurian action game Tides of Annihilation, confirmed to host a hands-on demo booth at Hall 6, B-050 — one of the notable new Chinese single-player entrants. GamesWirtschaft's own Hall 6 tracker still doesn't list a stand number, but InvenGlobal and WorthPlaying both independently name the booth.

games.title: Tides of Annihilation
games.note: Expanded event-exclusive demo, Hall 6, booth B-050, running Aug 27–30.

crowdNote: High-profile trailer buzz but a single-title booth — moderate lines, spiking after any ONL appearance.
visitAdvice: If it appears at Opening Night Live, queue early the next morning before word spreads.

name: Indie Arena Booth
description: The world's biggest indie booth — 2026 theme 'Democratree: games for everyone': ~200 games from 182 developers across 41 countries, with publisher pods (11 bit, Fireshine, Headup, Wired Productions) and a Nintendo section with Switch/Switch 2 stations. Audio brand beyerdynamic is this year's 'First Presenter' sponsor, kitting out 230+ developer stations with MMX 300 PRO headsets and running a vinyl soundtrack listening station.

games.title: Stronghold 4
games.note: Firefly's castle-sim revival — a headline title of the booth.

games.title: Paralives
games.note: Highly wishlisted life sim — expect one of the longer indie lines.

games.title: Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault
games.note: Shopkeeping/roguelite sequel.

games.title: Neon Abyss 2
games.note: Punk action roguelite sequel.

games.title: Escape Academy 2: Back 2 School
games.note: Co-op escape-room sequel.

games.title: Unrailed 2: Back on Track
games.note: Chaotic co-op track-building.

games.title: Hidden Folks 2
games.note: Hand-drawn hidden-object sequel.

games.title: Dungeon Clawler
games.note: Claw-machine deckbuilder.

games.title: We Were Here Tomorrow
games.note: Co-op puzzle series entry.

games.title: The 9th Dragon
games.note: Voxel close-quarters action.

games.title: Crowded
games.note: City-builder where crows are the units.

crowdNote: Busy but far more bearable than AAA halls; short rotating lines per station, worst Saturday afternoon.
visitAdvice: Thu/Fri morning is ideal. Browse the lineup on indiearena.org or the IAB Steam curator page beforehand and pick targets — devs are at their stations, so it's the best place to actually talk to the people making the games. Combine with the Retro & Family area in the same hall.

name: Korea Pavilion (KOCCA)
description: Umbrella pavilion organized by the Korea Creative Content Agency, bundling small and mid-size Korean studios in the indie area (plus a B2B zone) — the best single stop for discovering Korean PC/mobile titles beyond Krafton and Pearl Abyss.

games.title: Various Korean indie/mobile titles
games.note: Rotating multi-studio showcase; individual titles announced closer to the show.

crowdNote: Pavilion format spreads visitors across many small stands — walk-up friendly.
visitAdvice: Browse any time of day; a good low-queue option even on the weekend.

name: Koei Tecmo
description: Officially listed with a small Hall 10.2 stand, registered alongside Japanese partner Gentle Giants — the program is unannounced, and Koei Tecmo's main autumn stage is Tokyo Game Show. With Attack on Titan 3 due winter 2026, some presence for it is plausible but unconfirmed.

games.title: Attack on Titan 3
games.note: Winter 2026 release timing makes a showing plausible — our inference, nothing announced.

crowdNote: Small stand in the indie/merch hall — browsing traffic unless something playable turns up.
visitAdvice: Check on-site: a playable Attack on Titan 3 or Nioh 3 station would queue fast; otherwise a quick stop on your Indie Arena Booth round.

name: Bilibili
description: Chinese video/community platform and game publisher, confirmed in the official directory with a booth in the indie-focused Hall 10.1. Its 2026 game lineup hasn't been announced yet.

games.title: Bilibili-published titles (lineup TBA)
games.note: Expect an indie-scale showcase similar to prior years.

crowdNote: Modest indie-area booth; short waits except during signing/creator events.
visitAdvice: Easy walk-up while touring the indie hall; check the app on-site for stage or giveaway schedules.

name: Aternos
description: The free Minecraft server host (Bonn-based, one of the largest in the world) runs 'MC Party' together with the Cytooxien team: four custom-built Minecraft minigames — Dragon Escape, Farming, Dungeons and Paintball — played solo or in groups via a player-card queue system. Rounds earn coins to trade at the booth for Aternos/Cytooxien merch and MGA's Miniverse 'Make It Mini Minecraft' collectibles.

games.title: MC Party (Minecraft minigames)
games.note: Dragon Escape, Farming, Dungeons and Paintball — every round earns coins redeemable for merch and prizes.

crowdNote: Minecraft pulls kids and families hard — steady queues for minigame rounds, heaviest on the weekend family days.
visitAdvice: Grab a player card early and drop into rounds between hall runs — coins accumulate across the day, so split visits work well. Hall 10.1 is calmest in the morning.

name: Behaviour Interactive
description: Dead by Daylight's studio is officially listed with a Hall 10.1 stand in the game's 10th-anniversary year. Its booth program is still unannounced — expect anniversary content and community activities rather than a AAA-style demo floor.

games.title: Dead by Daylight
games.note: Nothing officially announced for the stand yet; anniversary-year community presence is the safe bet.

crowdNote: 60M+ players and a devoted community — steady lines if meet-and-greets or photo ops run.
visitAdvice: Check DbD's socials during the show for timed community events; otherwise an easy drop-in between Hall 10 indie sessions.

name: SCS Software
description: The Euro Truck Simulator 2 / American Truck Simulator studio brings its traditional community stand — truck-seat driving rigs, team meet-and-greets and merch, a gamescom fixture for years (plus a business-area stand in Hall 4.1).

games.title: Euro Truck Simulator 2
games.note: Driving rigs are the stand's tradition; specific 2026 program unannounced.

games.title: American Truck Simulator
games.note: Usually shown alongside ETS2 on the rigs.

crowdNote: Limited driving rigs mean moderate rotating queues; fans linger to chat with the team.
visitAdvice: Rigs turn over slowly — come at hall opening if you want seat time.

name: Bloober Team
description: The Silent Hill 2 remake and Cronos: The New Dawn studio is officially listed in Hall 10.1 (plus a business-area stand); its 2026 booth program is unannounced — Cronos content or a look at its next horror project are the plausible showings. Cronos art also features in Tencent's offsite Worlds of Play exhibition.

games.title: Cronos: The New Dawn
games.note: Nothing announced for the stand yet; Bloober's flagship since its Sept 2025 release.

crowdNote: A small stand with a devoted horror crowd — short lines unless a new reveal drops at ONL.
visitAdvice: If Bloober shows anything at Opening Night Live, expect the stand to spike the next morning — otherwise a quick stop.

name: Coffee Stain
description: The Satisfactory studio and publisher of Valheim and Deep Rock Galactic is officially listed with a Hall 10.1 stand; its program is unannounced. Satisfactory's 1.2 update shipped in June and an official Satisfactory board game is due late 2026 — demo stations and merch are the safe bets.

games.title: Satisfactory
games.note: Nothing announced for the stand yet; the 1.2 update (June 2026) makes it the obvious centerpiece.

crowdNote: Beloved catalog but a low-key stand — browsing traffic more than queues.
visitAdvice: Easy drop-in next to the other Hall 10.1 publisher stands (SCS, Bloober, Kepler).

name: Kepler Interactive
description: The publisher collective behind Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 lists ONTOS as its featured gamescom product: Frictional Games' (SOMA, Amnesia) sci-fi narrative mystery aboard the repurposed moon hotel Samsara, due 2026. Expect a presentation-style stand rather than a mass demo floor.

games.title: ONTOS
games.note: SOMA spiritual successor from Frictional Games, releasing 2026; listed on Kepler's official gamescom profile.

crowdNote: Strong word-of-mouth brand but a small Hall 10.1 stand — short lines except right after any stage or ONL showing.
visitAdvice: Pair with the Indie Arena Booth one level up; afternoons are quieter once the epix school groups thin out.

name: Atari
description: Anchor of Hall 10.1's retro corner: Atari's stand sits in a cluster with the revived Commodore (C059/B050) and MicroProse (A060/B061) — expect classic and modern-retro hardware, re-releases and collector merch across all three.
crowdNote: Browsing traffic and nostalgic dwell time rather than queues.
visitAdvice: A good low-energy stop while sitting out peak queues elsewhere; merch lines grow on Saturday.

name: LEGO Games
description: Multi-stand block in Hall 9.1 next to Nintendo, confirmed returning for 2026. The lineup is TBC — the 2025 booth featured Batman, One Piece and Super Mario activations, so expect current LEGO video games plus set photo-ops.

games.title: LEGO video game lineup (TBC)
games.note: LEGO historically reveals new games at gamescom/ONL; 2026 titles unannounced.

crowdNote: Family magnet in the same hall as Nintendo — photo-op and demo lines get long on the weekend.
visitAdvice: Weekday mornings; weekends are dominated by families.

name: Magic: The Gathering (Wizards of the Coast)
description: Wizards of the Coast anchors the trading-card corner of Hall 5.2, sharing its stand block with European distributor ADC Blackfire. Learn-to-play tables and 2026-set demos are the safe bet (this year's slate includes Reality Fracture and previews of The Hobbit crossover). Konami's separate Yu-Gi-Oh! stand, Ravensburger, Pegasus and Panini fill out the same hall.

games.title: Magic: The Gathering
games.note: Learn-to-play and casual play tables; promo cards usually while daily stocks last.

crowdNote: The card-game hall gets dense on public days, and promo giveaways cause morning rushes.
visitAdvice: Morning for promos, late afternoon for a relaxed learn-to-play seat.

name: ASUS ROG
description: Large Hall 8.1 presence plus an outdoor activation at Hall 8 North: ROG laptops, monitors and the ROG Xbox Ally handheld family playable on-site.
crowdNote: ROG handheld try-out stations build 15–45 min lines; the rest flows freely.
visitAdvice: Morning visit if you want hands-on time with the ROG Ally handhelds.

name: Samsung Odyssey
description: Odyssey gaming monitors and SSDs with partner-game demo stations in Hall 9.1. Samsung's own stand is B020/C029 (an earlier revision had this swapped with Pearl Abyss's booth); it is additionally co-registered at Pearl Abyss's B010/C011 stand, which it powers with 6K Odyssey G8 displays.
crowdNote: Big footprint and Hall 9 foot traffic keep it busy, but station turnover is fast.
visitAdvice: Combine with your Nintendo Hall 9 visit; no need to rush it at opening.

name: Razer
description: Two official locations (Hall 10.2 consumer + Hall 2.2 business). Hands-on with the 2026 peripheral line following its big CES slate, esports activations and merch drops.
crowdNote: Solid fan traffic for limited merch and giveaway drops, but nothing like platform-holder queues.
visitAdvice: For limited merch, go early on the first public day; otherwise any weekday afternoon.

name: Logitech G
description: Official directory listing under Logitech and Logitech G (second stand in Hall 10.1): gaming mice, keyboards, headsets and sim-racing rigs with try-before-you-buy stations.
crowdNote: Browse-through booth; only sim-racing rigs generate short waits.
visitAdvice: Any time works; sim rigs are quietest weekday mornings.

name: AGON by AOC
description: AOC's gaming-monitor brand with its latest high-refresh OLED and Mini-LED monitors on demo stations.
crowdNote: Low-queue browse stop.
visitAdvice: Walk in anytime; pairs well with Logitech and ASUS in the same hall.

name: AMD
description: Co-registered on a shared Hall 7.1 stand block with Webedia's community area, Vodafone, ZOTAC and the Driveball Arena — expect Ryzen/Radeon demo rigs powering partner activations rather than a standalone AMD mega-booth. AMD also hosts its own Cologne event on Aug 23, teasing a Radeon announcement right before the show.
crowdNote: Traffic on the shared block follows the community-stage program and creator meetups more than AMD itself.
visitAdvice: Worth a pass if you're PC-hardware shopping; check the community area's stage schedule for creator sessions.

name: Wargaming
description: Confirmed NOT exhibiting on the show floor for 2026 — GamesWirtschaft's exhibitor ticker lists Wargaming under cancellations, dropping the Hall 1 Event Arena presence it had in 2025. The only confirmed 2026 presence is the offsite Wargaming Community Party on Aug 28 at HERBRAND's Ehrenfeld (~€10, Eventbrite) covering WoT, WoWs, Blitz and World of Tanks: HEAT. The official directory lists only B2B stands in trade halls 3.2 and 2.2 — nothing in the Entertainment Area, consistent with the cancellation.

games.title: World of Tanks / Warships / HEAT
games.note: No show-floor demo booth in 2026 — appearing only at the offsite Community Party (Aug 28), not the official Entertainment Area.

crowdNote: No show-floor booth in 2026, so nothing to queue for on-site; the offsite party is ticketed and capped separately.
visitAdvice: Skip the show floor for Wargaming — grab Community Party tickets on Eventbrite early if you're a player, since it's capped.

name: Kuro Games
description: Wuthering Waves developer exhibited in 2024 and 2025 but has made no gamescom 2026 announcement — attendance looks doubtful; its current focus is the WuWa 3.6 broadcast and the new Elysium anime.

games.title: Wuthering Waves
games.note: Expected only from past-year patterns; no 2026 booth confirmed.

crowdNote: Nothing confirmed to queue for; if a booth materializes expect HoYoverse-style merch crowds.
visitAdvice: Don't plan around Kuro Games; re-check the official directory and @Wuthering_Waves socials in the final two weeks.

name: Take-Two / Rockstar (GTA 6)
description: No consumer booth: Take-Two's only registration in the official directory is a shared industry stand in business Hall 4.1 (trade only). The GTA 6 moment happens off-site: an 'Extended Look' premieres on Netflix on Thursday Aug 27 (YouTube six hours later), deliberately timed to gamescom week. GTA 6 launches Nov 19, 2026.

games.title: Grand Theft Auto VI — Extended Look
games.note: Streaming showcase on Netflix Aug 27, 3pm ET — not at the show.

games.title: NBA 2K27 / 2K catalog
games.note: 2K exhibited in 2025 but has made no 2026 announcement.

crowdNote: No confirmed physical presence.
visitAdvice: Watch the GTA 6 Extended Look on Netflix/YouTube on Aug 27 during the show; keep an eye on late exhibitor updates in case 2K books space.

name: THQ Nordic
description: NOT attending — officially cancelled its gamescom 2026 presence (July 8), citing a lack of showcase-ready titles; hopes to return 2027. Its Digital Showcase on Aug 7 (Titan Quest II, Wreckfest 2, Gothic Remake) replaces the physical showing.

games.title: Titan Quest II / Wreckfest 2 / Gothic Remake
games.note: Digital Showcase (streamed Aug 7) only — no gamescom booth.

crowdNote: No booth.
visitAdvice: Watch the THQ Nordic Digital Showcase stream instead; partner titles may still surface at other booths.

name: Paradox / Urban Games
description: No classic solo booth: Paradox co-presents Transport Fever 3 with Urban Games, whose stand is officially confirmed at Hall 8.1, B053a — complete with a London double-decker bus as the eye-catcher. Paradox itself is registered in the directory at Level Infinite's shared Hall 6.1 stand, so a presence in the Tencent area looks likely.

games.title: Transport Fever 3
games.note: Shown with Urban Games in Hall 8; double-decker photo op.

games.title: Paradox grand-strategy catalog
games.note: Paradox's own directory registration sits at Level Infinite's Hall 6.1 stand; nothing specific announced about what it shows there.

crowdNote: Niche-but-devoted audience — steady sim fans rather than mass queues.
visitAdvice: Queues reasonable even at peak; combine with CDPR and Square Enix in the same hall.
